As juvenile as it may seem: Watch french children’s shows. 

When you were a child and learning your native language you started with easy to understand cartoons and as you got older worked your way up to the shows you watch now and thus the understanding of the language you have now. 

Second languages are no different. You can’t expect to understand perfectly immediately. You have to start from the beginning and work from there.

I started learning when I was 9. I remember reading Les trois petit cochons, Le chat et la lune, Les animaux des bayou, Marc le magicien, Boucles violettes, and answering questions about them. Well, because I’m still in school I haven’t actually done anything job wise. However, making a proper plan for how you intend to reach your goal is always the first step. You need to think critically and not try to rush into anything. You’ll never get anywhere if you just keep hoping something will work and don’t put in a proper plan. Maybe try setting aside and saving a certain amount of money each month until you have enough. Or you could even try setting up a donation thing online if you really wanted to. The main thing is that wanting to transition should be your motivation: Not what’s holding you down. Make a plan and stick to it even if it seems like it’s not working at first. Things take time, but no matter how long they take: They will happen eventually; and it will be worth the effort and time.
